key_insight: This pilot study presents the first cross‑provincial evaluation showing that adapting BCCRTron, a domain‑adapted transformer for pathology reports, enables more reliable transfer of cancer‑registry NLP models across Canadian jurisdictions with differing reporting conventions.
problem_solved: Population‑based cancer registries rely on manual abstraction from pathology reports, which is slow and resource‑intensive. The paper addresses whether transformer‑based registry NLP models can generalize across provinces with heterogeneous reporting styles and how to adapt them to new jurisdictions.
method: Use BCCRTron (a domain‑adapted transformer) as the base model for extracting diagnostic information from pathology reports.
Perform cross‑provincial adaptation and evaluation: transfer the model between registry datasets from different provinces and measure performance changes.
Compare adaptation strategies (e.g., fine‑tuning on target jurisdiction data and targeted domain adaptation) to quantify gains in accuracy and robustness.
impact: Demonstrates that targeted model adaptation enables practical deployment of registry NLP systems across jurisdictions, reducing manual abstraction burden and highlighting the necessity of cross‑jurisdiction validation for clinical NLP models.
visual_elements: Map of Canada with arrows showing model transfer between provinces and small performance indicators per province
Bar chart comparing model performance before and after adaptation for each province
Pipeline diagram: pathology report → BCCRTron (pretrained) → adaptation/fine‑tuning → extracted registry fields
Icon set: pathology report, clock (time saved), shield (data/validation), and model weights (transfer learning)
paper_title: Adapting Natural Language Processing Models Across Jurisdictions: A pilot Study in Canadian Cancer Registries
paper_authors: Jonathan Simkin, Lovedeep Gondara, Zeeshan Rizvi, Gregory Doyle, Jeff Dowden
